analysis:
The only units supplied were base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/cache-aware-routing.md (base lines 1-910, header 'Last updated: 2026-10-08'). No patch hunks and no head_text were included, so I could not identify what this PR changed. Coverage is limited to the base excerpt; the tail of the file after line 910 and the diff itself were not seen. No security regression can be asserted from them, so findings are empty.

Base doc claims the next pass should check against the actual diff, if one appears:
- Cache scope is a coordinator-authored HMAC over account, model build, aggregate hash, prompt contract and block-hash contract (cache_route_keys.go lines ~211-218). Caller prompt_cache_key and user fields must not participate. This supports the T-041 / SEC-035 account isolation claim.
- Routing evidence comes only from provider-authenticated v2 receipts. Mismatches fence the capability for 60s, doubling up to 10min. Holders are bounded: 4 per bucket, 250k global, TTL at most 30min, resident TTL 30s.
- Cache routing is default-off. A revoked owner at writer dequeue falls back to ordinary cold inference.
- Persistence stores only HMAC-derived keys; route and scope keys are never persisted.
- GET /v1/cache/status exposes aggregate counters only (no model IDs, providers, accounts, scopes or paths at lines ~910+). Any added labels would be an information-disclosure risk (T-051, T-058).
- SSD tier: TTL stays at 30 minutes and the disk budget/reserve policy is unchanged. Raising the TTL needs a fresh SEC-035 sign-off (T-041). Operator-selected external volumes are still outside the attested boundary.

If the PR only edits prose, verify it does not overstate the guarantees above (for example claiming production deployment or live measurements).
